title: SSDs and 4D v11 SQL
author: Josh Fletcher, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: SSD architecture (flash cells, controllers, write amplification)
Benchmarking (500,000 record modification, random Goto Record, 6,000,000 record sort)

historical_commentary.text: This note explains early-generation SSD internals (flash cells, controllers, write amplification, fragmentation-related performance degradation) and benchmarks specific 2009-2010 consumer/enterprise drives (Western Digital Raptor, Intel X25-M, OCZ Colossus) against 4D disk-intensive workloads. The core recommendation — that 4D benefits substantially from fast storage because indexes, the data file, the data log, and the cache are all disk-bound — remains valid today, but the specific hardware, controller behavior, and degradation characteristics described are obsolete: modern SSDs (NVMe, TRIM support, wear-leveling improvements) have moved far beyond the drives and controller generation profiled here, so the benchmark data and buying advice are of historical interest only.
related_updates: Modern NVMe SSDs with TRIM and mature wear-leveling have superseded the early SATA SSD generation (Intel X25-M, OCZ Colossus) benchmarked in this note
4D's general guidance to use fast storage remains valid, but should be based on current storage benchmarks, not this decade-old hardware comparison
